title: Pelvic Girdle Pain and Sacroiliac-region Pain
case: Case: A woman at 28 weeks of pregnancy has pain at the back of the pelvis on both sides. Pain is worse when climbing stairs and rolling in bed. No bleeding, no headache, no leg swelling. ASLR is painful on the right and eased when a belt is applied. Thigh thrust reproduces her familiar pain on the right. Neurological exam is normal.

Working diagnosis: pregnancy-related pelvic girdle pain. Plan: education, a pelvic belt trial, avoidance of aggravating positions, gentle glute and trunk exercises, and review in 1 to 2 weeks, with a clear plan to refer for any warning sign.

differentials.name: Lumbar facet or non-specific back pain
differentials.key: Pain above L5, extension or flexion provocation

differentials.name: Gluteal tendinopathy
differentials.key: Lateral hip pain, lying on that side

differentials.name: Axial spondyloarthritis
differentials.key: Under 40, insidious, night and morning pain, better with exercise

differentials.name: Sacral or pelvic stress fracture
differentials.key: Sharp pain with weight-bearing, endurance runners, low energy availability, postpartum or osteoporosis

differentials.name: Septic sacroiliitis
differentials.key: Fever, severe pain, unable to weight-bear

differentials.name: Visceral pain (urinary tract, ovarian, ectopic pregnancy)

qa: Why does relief with the belt matter? It suggests that the pelvis load transfer is part of the problem and that supportive measures may help. It does not prove which structure is the source.

Why not use forceful provocation tests in pregnancy? Because they can cause pain that lasts and the patient and baby deserve the lowest necessary risk. Gentle versions and a good history are usually enough.
Fever with severe sacroiliac pain and inability to bear weight. What do you do? Refer urgently the same day because infection is possible.
Why must hip pain be separated from SIJ pain? Groin and hip rotation pain lead to a different diagnosis and treatment pathway.
Why avoid saying the pelvis is out of place? The claim is not supported by good evidence, and it can create fear and unnecessary dependence on treatment.

tests.name: Thigh thrust (posterior pelvic pain provocation, P4)

fields.Purpose: Apply a posterior shear force to the SIJ through the femur
fields.Patient position: Supine, hip flexed to about 90 degrees, knee bent
fields.Therapist position: Standing on the side being tested; one hand under the sacrum for support, the other holding the knee and thigh
fields.Action: Apply a firm posterior force through the long axis of the femur with the other hand stabilising the pelvis; build force gradually
fields.Positive: Reproduction of the patient's familiar posterior pelvic pain
fields.Supports: May indicate SIJ-region pain when combined with other tests
fields.Limits: A negative test does not exclude the SIJ. Groin pain suggests the hip
fields.Errors: Applying force too quickly; allowing the pelvis to rotate; confusing groin or buttock muscle pain with SIJ pain
fields.Pregnancy: Use only gentle force; stop if painful or if the patient feels unwell

fields.Purpose: Assess the ability of the pelvis to transfer load in a simple lifting task
fields.Action: Ask the patient to lift one leg about 20 cm from the bed, one at a time; ask about difficulty and pain
fields.Positive: Pain or a feeling of heaviness or difficulty lifting the leg; relief when the pelvis is gently compressed by the therapist or a belt
fields.Supports: Impaired load transfer in the pelvis, particularly in pregnancy-related pain

fields.Position and action: Supine; therapist crosses arms and presses outward and down on both anterior superior iliac spines
fields.Positive: Familiar pain in the SIJ area

fields.Position and action: Supine at the edge of the bed; one leg hangs off, other hip held in flexion; gentle extension force on the hanging leg
fields.Positive: Familiar pain in the SIJ area

fields.Position and action: Side-lying; downward force through the top of the iliac crest
fields.Positive: Familiar pain in the SIJ area

fields.Position and action: Prone; downward force through the sacrum
fields.Positive: Familiar pain in the SIJ area

redFlags.Finding: Vaginal bleeding, severe abdominal pain, leaking fluid, regular contractions in pregnancy
redFlags.Possible concern (not confirmed): Placental problem, preterm labour, ectopic pregnancy

redFlags.Finding: Severe headache with visual disturbance, sudden swelling, upper abdominal pain in pregnancy
Calf swelling, warmth, pain or sudden breathlessness
Fever with severe pelvic pain, cannot bear weight
Sudden severe pain after a fall or impact, or pain with weight-bearing in a runner or postpartum
redFlags.Possible concern (not confirmed): Sacral or pubic ramus stress fracture

redFlags.Finding: Saddle numbness, bladder or bowel change
Visible gap or severe locking at the pubic symphysis with inability to walk

manual.name: Gentle SIJ mobilization or muscle energy technique
manual.finding: Positive provocation cluster, restricted comfort in a hip or pelvic movement
manual.application: Supine or side-lying, low-grade oscillations or gentle isometric contractions

manual.name: Soft-tissue work to gluteal and hip muscles

manualNotes: Preferred starting choice: education and a graded stabilisation and strengthening program. Manual therapy is optional for short-term relief. Do not claim to correct a pelvic misalignment or out-of-place bone; the evidence for that explanation is not credible. Avoid high-velocity thrusts in pregnancy.

exercise.Steps: Lying or sitting, gently draw the lower abdomen in without holding the breath
Lying with knees bent, lift hips
Lying on the side, knees bent, lift the upper knee
Hold a support, lift one foot
Standing with support, lift the leg sideways

exerciseNotes: Pelvic belt: a belt can give support during activity and may reduce pain for some patients. It is a symptom aid, not a cure. Position it low, around the hips below the anterior superior iliac spines, snug but comfortable.

Daily-life advice: avoid wide leg positions, carrying loads on one side, long single-leg standing and stair climbing when avoidable; roll in bed with knees together; use a pillow between the knees; sit to dress.
Symptom rule: mild discomfort that settles within a short time is acceptable. Sharp pain, pain lasting after exercise, or any pregnancy warning sign means stop.

modalities.name: Acupuncture
modalities.indicated: Option in some guidelines for pregnancy-related PGP

pathway: Any emergency or urgent flag? Yes: act as in Section G.
Lumbar or hip source clearly responsible? Yes: use that pathway.
Posterior pelvic pain below L5, task-related pain, a positive provocation cluster or ASLR? Yes: working diagnosis is pelvic girdle pain (SIJ-region).
Pubic symphysis pain with tenderness? Working diagnosis includes symphysis involvement.
Persistent severe pain or no improvement with active care? Medical review.
Visit 1: screen for red flags and pregnancy complications, explain that PGP is common and not harmful to the baby, give practical advice.
Early: reduce painful tasks, belt trial, gentle exercises, optional manual therapy.
Middle: progress stabilisation and strengthening to functional tasks.
